etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English born, boren, borne, iborne, from Old English boren, ġeboren, from Proto-West Germanic *boran, *gaboran, from Proto-Germanic *buranaz, past participle of Proto-Germanic *beraną (“to bear, carry”), equivalent to bear +‎ -en. Cognate with Saterland Frisian gebooren (“born”), West Frisian berne (“born”), Dutch geboren (“born”), German geboren (“born”), Swedish boren (“born”).

definitions.definition: past participle of bear; given birth to.
(obsolete) past participle of bear in other senses.

quote.citation: 1784, Thomas Sheridan, Life of Dr. Swift, Section I:
quote.text: In some monasteries the severity of the clausure is hard to be born.

quote.citation: 1815 December (indicated as 1816), [Jane Austen], chapter XVI, in Emma: […], volume I, London:  […]  [Charles Roworth and James Moyes] for John Murray, →OCLC, page 286:
quote.text: If I had not persuaded Harriet into liking the man, I could have born any thing.

definitions.definition: Having from birth (or as if from birth) a certain quality or character; innate; inherited.

quote.citation: 1701 January (indicated as 1700), [Daniel Defoe], “Part II”, in The True-Born Englishman. A Satyr, [London: s.n.], →OCLC, page 61:
quote.text: I'll make it out, deny it he that can, / His Worship is a True-born Engliſhman, / In all the Latitude that Empty Word / By Modern Acceptation's understood.

quote.citation: 1942, Storm Jameson, Then we shall hear singing: a fantasy in C major:
quote.text: I ought really to have called him my sergeant. He's a born sergeant. That's as much as to say he's a born scoundrel.

quote.citation: 1965, Frank Herbert, Dune‎[1] (Science Fiction), New York: Ace Books, →OCLC, page 118‎[2]:
quote.text: “Your desert boots are fitted slip-fashion at the ankles. Who told you to do that?”"It . . . seemed the right way.""That it most certainly is."And Kynes rubbed his cheek, thinking of the legend: "He shall know your ways as though born to them."

definitions.definition: (Geordie) Alternative spelling of burn (with fire etc.)
